content.value_statement: Architecture decisions often lack explicit constraints, alternatives, and traceability. This skill structures requirements, compares designs, creates diagrams, and records decisions for implementation teams.
actual_capabilities: Translate business goals and nonfunctional requirements into service, data, deployment, and security architecture.
Compare architecture styles and technologies using performance, cost, complexity, community, and team-fit criteria.
Produce C4, UML, deployment, network, data-flow, and entity-relationship diagrams in Mermaid or PlantUML.
Draft ADRs with context, decisions, alternatives, consequences, and explicit trade-offs.
Review codebase boundaries, dependencies, architecture style, technical debt, and architectural compliance.
Create Markdown architecture, API, deployment documents, and phased implementation plans.
limitations: The skill designs systems but does not deploy, configure, or operate production environments.
Grounded codebase analysis requires access to relevant source files and project constraints.
Mermaid and PlantUML outputs may require separate rendering and visual validation.
The ecommerce reference is illustrative and does not validate business, legal, fairness, or compliance assumptions.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Architecture
use_cases.description: Define service boundaries, data ownership, integrations, deployment topology, risks, and phased delivery for a new product.

use_cases.title: Review an Existing Codebase
use_cases.description: Map modules and dependencies, identify architectural drift, and prioritize changes with evidence and trade-offs.

use_cases.title: Standardize Technical Decisions
use_cases.description: Compare technologies, document ADRs, and create C4 views that implementation and operations teams can review.

prompt_templates.title: Outline a System
prompt_templates.prompt: Outline an architecture for [product]. Ask for missing users, scale, integrations, security, availability, budget, and team constraints before recommending a design.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Technologies
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [option A] and [option B] for [workload]. Evaluate fit, performance, operations, cost, maturity, migration risk, and team experience.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Codebase
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository's architecture. Map modules and dependencies, identify boundary violations and technical debt, then propose prioritized improvements with validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design from Business Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these business rules into a domain model and system architecture. Provide alternatives, C4 views, data ownership, failure modes, ADRs, and phased delivery.

output_examples.input: Design a multi-region appointment platform for clinics with strict availability and privacy requirements.
output: Recommended regional service architecture with explicit data ownership and failover boundaries.
C4 context and container views covering identity, scheduling, notifications, and payment integrations.
ADRs for consistency, regional failover, and event delivery, with risks and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Compare Kafka and RabbitMQ for asynchronous order processing.
output: Decision matrix covering delivery semantics, throughput, routing, replay, operations, ecosystem maturity, and cost.
Workload-specific recommendation with rejected alternatives, assumptions, and proof-of-concept criteria.

output_examples.input: Review a modular monolith that has circular dependencies and unclear ownership.
output: Module and dependency map identifying cycles, shared-state coupling, and boundary violations.
Prioritized remediation plan with ownership boundaries, migration stages, risks, and measurable completion criteria.

best_practices: Provide business goals, workload estimates, compliance needs, budget, team skills, and existing technology constraints.
Request alternatives and explicit trade-offs before accepting a recommended architecture.
Validate generated diagrams, assumptions, and ADRs with implementation, security, data, and operations stakeholders.
anti_patterns: Do not select technology based only on popularity without workload and team evidence.
Do not treat illustrative scoring models or estimates as validated production policy.
Do not accept architecture diagrams without ownership, data flow, failure behavior, and operational boundaries.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide users, workflows, scale, latency, availability, security, compliance, integrations, budget, team skills, and existing technology constraints.

faq.question: Can it analyze an existing repository?
faq.answer: Yes. It can map modules, dependencies, architecture style, technical debt, and compliance when relevant source files are available.

faq.question: Which diagram formats does it support?
faq.answer: It can produce C4, UML, deployment, network, data-flow, and entity-relationship diagrams using Mermaid or PlantUML.

faq.question: Does it deploy the proposed architecture?
faq.answer: No. It produces designs, decisions, diagrams, and documents, while implementation and production operations remain separate work.

faq.question: Can it create architecture decision records?
faq.answer: Yes. It structures ADRs around context, status, decision, alternatives, consequences, risks, and trade-offs.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
